# Stream Overlays

> Browser overlays for streamers: read your hardware in the browser via the Gamepad API,
> draw it to a transparent canvas, and composite over your scene in OBS. Static files only,
> configuration in the URL — no install, no accounts, no server. The first vertical is sim
> racing: live throttle/brake/clutch/steering from a Logitech G923, as a catalogue of small
> canvas overlays. Currently a pilot: the engine and module architecture are built and
> tested; three overlays are migrated, the rest of the 72-overlay catalogue is pending.

## What it is

- **Static-first.** Overlays are plain HTML/JS served over HTTP; the browser reads the wheel
  client-side, so nothing leaves the user's machine and there is nothing to host but files.
- **Config in the URL.** `?style=<id>&scale=<n>` — portable, shareable, bookmarkable. No storage.
- **Layered architecture.** Pure logic (calibration maths, demo lap) with no DOM; a browser
  runtime (gamepad seam, calibration engine, draw kit, loop); one module per overlay exporting
  `id` + `draw(ctx,w,h,state,mem)`; thin pages that wire it together.
- **The manifest is the source of truth.** `catalogue.json` carries every overlay's id, name,
  size, set, stage, and channels; `set`/`uses` are derived from the draw code and verified.

## Install

- Requires only a static HTTP server (the Gamepad API and ES modules need an HTTP context).
- Clone: https://github.com/dberardi2020/stream-overlays
- Serve `overlays/sim-racing` and open `pages/gallery.html` to browse every overlay over a demo lap, or `pages/overlay.html?style=bowtie` for one live.
- In OBS: Browser Source → Interact → press a wheel button → calibrate.
